novel_mechanics_found: su15 is a fruit-merge/delivery game driven entirely by ACTION6 clicks. Core physics measured: a click pulls every fruit within radius ~8 of the click point toward it by min(~8px, distance); two same-tier fruits pulled to the same point MERGE into the next tier (a=1px -> 6=2x2 -> f=3x3 -> b=4x4, mass-doubling each tier). Tier chips in the top-left corner display the progression; hollow boxes at the top are GOAL DISPLAYS (which fruits to produce), NOT drop zones - the actual delivery targets are the big 9-colored round BLOBS on the field (L3 breakthrough: b-fruit onto the left blob + f-fruit onto the right blob fired the win; blob order matches the goal-display order). Row 63 is a RESOURCE METER (64 px): successful drags cost ~1-2, but FAILED clicks cost 3-13 with escalation; meter exhaustion = GAME_OVER. Failed clicks happen when a click catches two different-tier fruits in its ~8-10 radius (only merge-pairs may share a click), when the drag path would clip the field boundary diagonally, and after repeated failures (an escalating lockout that must be waited out). env.reset() restarts the CURRENT level fresh (level count persists) - the recovery loop for a botched board. L4 introduces a HUNTER (7-colored ~8px sprite): it patrols toward the current biggest/nearest fruit at ~4px per player click and on contact DEGRADES the fruit one tier (halving its mass); L4 gives exactly 8 unit-fruits for an 8-unit b-fruit goal, so ANY hunter contact makes the level unwinnable - it ate 1-3 units in all four attempted runs (best line: 14-click blob-ward merge-cascade). The hunter walks freely onto the blob (no sanctuary), ignores clicks, and cannot be dragged.
gotchas: Deliver to the BLOBS, not the top boxes: the top hollow boxes are goal displays; L3 win = b-fruit overlapping the left blob AND f-fruit overlapping the right blob (partial overlap sufficed; order matches display order).

Click radius ~8 for the drag pull, but interference radius is larger (~9-10.5): a click within ~10 of a second different-tier fruit FAILS and burns escalating meter (3-13 px per fail). Keep every click >=10.5 from any fruit you are not moving; equal-tier pairs are exempt (that is how merges work).
Merge-point must be within 8 of BOTH fruits - double-check with exact distances; an 8.6 slips out of radius and the click half-fails (one fruit pulled, no merge).
Merges are free transport: place merge points displaced toward the destination - each tier merge gives both fruits up to 8px of travel.
Diagonal drags whose endpoint would clip the top boundary get rejected; decompose into axis moves near edges. Fruits rest flush at row 10 (field rows 10-62).
Failed clicks escalate: after 2-3 fails on the same fruit it locks up for many clicks (rest clicks do not reliably clear it). NEVER retry a failed click immediately.

env.reset() restarts the current level with a fresh 64px meter and pristine layout; levels_completed persists. Deliberately exhausting the meter (repeat an expensive failing click) also forces GAME_OVER then reset works the same.
CAUTION: after env.reset() do NOT replay the L1/L2 prefix - the game resumes at the current level; replaying stray clicks scrambles the fresh board (cost one full meter learning this).

L4 hunter: spawns top-right ~(20,54), moves ~4px per click (any click, including neutral ones), beelines the biggest fruit, degrades on contact (f->6, 6->a). With exactly 8 units for an 8-unit goal, zero contact is survivable. Blobs are NOT sanctuary. Not clickable/draggable. Untested counters: body-blocking with the b (b hops 8px/click > hunter 4px/click, so a completed b can outrun it to the blob), luring with a deliberately-built decoy while assembling elsewhere (no spare mass though), or an unknown anti-hunter mechanic.

L4 candidate line for a future attempt (14 clicks, died only to hunter contact): merge pairs at displaced points (33,32),(28,52),(7,32),(6,48); six-merges (27,41)/(27,46) and (6,39)/(5,44); f-hops along board edges; final b-merge on the blob. Two runs lost exactly 1-2 units to grazing - a luckier/tighter route may clear it.

narrative: Replayed the banked 21-action L1+L2 line, then spent the session reverse-engineering the drag/merge physics: pull radius, min-8px moves, merge-as-transport, the row-63 resource meter with escalating fail costs, the click-interference rule, and boundary-clip rejection. First L3 attempt died to meter exhaustion from repeated finale fails (both delivery spots poison each other click-wise under the interference radius); the breakthrough was realizing the top boxes are only goal displays and the ignored 9-colored blobs are the real delivery pods - after that, a 18-click line (merge cascade + interleaved deliveries to the two blobs) won L3 cleanly on the fifth board attempt. Gate-verified the full 39-action sequence (reached_level=3, reproduced=True).
